name: Google Cloud SDK
description: Protects against destructive gcloud operations like instances delete, \ sql instances delete, and gsutil rm -r

destructive_patterns.name: compute-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud compute instances delete permanently destroys VM instances.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
compute instances delete permanently destroys VMs:

- Instance is stopped and deleted
- Boot disk deleted (unless --keep-disks specified)
- External IPs released back to pool
- Instance metadata and logs lost

Use --keep-disks=boot,data to preserve disks for recovery.

destructive_patterns.name: disk-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud compute disks delete permanently destroys disk data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
compute disks delete permanently destroys persistent disks:

- All data on the disk is lost forever
- Cannot be recovered without snapshots
- Any instances using the disk will fail

Create a snapshot before deletion: gcloud compute disks snapshot DISK

destructive_patterns.name: sql-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud sql instances delete permanently destroys the Cloud SQL instance.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
sql instances delete permanently destroys Cloud SQL:

- Database and all data deleted
- All backups deleted (unless retained)
- Read replicas also deleted
- IP addresses released

Export data first: gcloud sql export sql INSTANCE gs://bucket/file.sql

destructive_patterns.name: gsutil-rm-recursive
destructive_patterns.description: gsutil rm -r permanently deletes all objects in the path.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
gsutil rm -r recursively deletes all objects:

- All objects under the path are deleted
- Cannot be recovered without versioning enabled
- -m flag parallelizes (faster but same risk)

List first: gsutil ls -r gs://bucket/path/ Enable versioning: gsutil versioning set on gs://bucket

destructive_patterns.name: gsutil-rb
destructive_patterns.description: gsutil rb removes the entire GCS bucket.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
gsutil rb removes the entire Cloud Storage bucket:

- Bucket must be empty (or use -f to force)
- Bucket name becomes available to others
- All bucket-level permissions lost

List contents first: gsutil ls gs://bucket/

destructive_patterns.name: gke-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud container clusters delete removes the entire GKE cluster.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
container clusters delete removes the entire GKE cluster:

- All nodes and workloads terminated
- Persistent volumes may be deleted
- Load balancers and IPs released
- Cluster-level secrets lost

Backup workloads: kubectl get all -A -o yaml > backup.yaml

destructive_patterns.name: project-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud projects delete removes the entire GCP project and ALL its resources!
destructive_patterns.explanation:
projects delete removes the ENTIRE GCP project:

- ALL resources in the project deleted
- All VMs, databases, storage, functions
- All IAM policies and service accounts
- 30-day recovery window, then permanent

This is the most destructive GCP command possible!

destructive_patterns.name: functions-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud functions delete removes the Cloud Function.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
functions delete removes Cloud Functions:

- Function code and configuration deleted
- Triggers and event subscriptions removed
- Function URL becomes unavailable

Export source first if not in version control.

destructive_patterns.name: pubsub-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud pubsub delete removes Pub/Sub topics or subscriptions.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
pubsub delete removes messaging infrastructure:

- Topic deletion removes all subscriptions
- Unacknowledged messages are lost
- Publishers will fail until recreated

Check subscribers: gcloud pubsub topics list-subscriptions TOPIC

destructive_patterns.name: firestore-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud firestore delete removes Firestore data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
firestore delete removes Firestore documents:

- Documents and collections deleted
- Subcollections may remain (delete recursively)
- No automatic backups by default

Export first: gcloud firestore export gs://bucket/backup

destructive_patterns.name: container-images-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud container images delete permanently deletes container images.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
container images delete removes images from GCR:

- Image tags and digests deleted
- Running containers unaffected (cached)
- New pulls will fail

List tags first: gcloud container images list-tags IMAGE

destructive_patterns.name: artifacts-docker-images-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud artifacts docker images delete permanently deletes container images.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
artifacts docker images delete removes images from Artifact Registry:

- Specified image version deleted
- Other tags pointing to same digest unaffected
- Consider cleanup policies instead

List versions: gcloud artifacts docker images list REPO

destructive_patterns.name: artifacts-repositories-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud artifacts repositories delete permanently deletes the repository.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
artifacts repositories delete removes entire repository:

- All packages/images in repository deleted
- Repository configuration lost
- IAM policies on repository removed

List contents: gcloud artifacts packages list --repository=REPO

destructive_patterns.name: secrets-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud secrets delete destroys a Secret Manager secret — credentials gone.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
secrets delete removes a Secret Manager secret:

- Secret and ALL its versions are permanently deleted
- No recovery window (unlike AWS Secrets Manager)
- Applications using the secret will fail to authenticate

List versions first: gcloud secrets versions list SECRET Disable rather than delete: gcloud secrets versions disable VERSION --secret=SECRET

destructive_patterns.name: kms-keys-destroy
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud kms keys versions destroy schedules a CryptoKeyVersion for destruction — data encrypted with it becomes unrecoverable.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
kms keys versions destroy scheduled destruction of a key version:

- 24-hour waiting period by default (per-keyring policy)
- After destruction: ALL data encrypted under this version is unrecoverable
- `gcloud kms keys versions restore` can undo within the waiting window

Consider `disable` instead if reversibility matters: gcloud kms keys versions disable VERSION --key=KEY --keyring=RING --location=LOC

destructive_patterns.name: iam-service-accounts-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud iam service-accounts delete removes a service account — workloads authenticating with it break.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
iam service-accounts delete removes a service account:

- Every workload using this SA loses access
- Keys associated with the SA are deleted
- CI/CD pipelines, GKE workloads, Cloud Functions dependent on this SA fail
- Can undelete within 30 days via `gcloud iam service-accounts undelete`

List usages first: gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy SA-EMAIL

destructive_patterns.name: iam-roles-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud iam roles delete removes a custom IAM role — all users/SAs bound to it lose the permissions.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
iam roles delete removes a custom IAM role:

- Every user/group/SA bound to this role loses its permissions
- Predefined roles cannot be deleted; this always targets custom roles
- Role is soft-deleted for 7 days, then permanently removed

Audit bindings first via gcloud projects get-iam-policy PROJECT

destructive_patterns.name: dns-managed-zones-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud dns managed-zones delete removes a DNS zone — domains stop resolving.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
dns managed-zones delete removes a Cloud DNS zone:

- All record sets in the zone are deleted
- Domains configured with this zone's nameservers stop resolving immediately
- Production traffic can go dark
- No undelete

Export records first: gcloud dns record-sets export zone-backup.yaml --zone=ZONE

destructive_patterns.name: logging-sinks-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud logging sinks delete removes an audit-log export — compliance/forensics impact.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
logging sinks delete stops log export to BigQuery/PubSub/Storage:

- Historical exports remain at the destination
- Future events stop flowing to the configured sink
- Compliance regimes (SOC2, ISO 27001) may require this sink

Consider disabling by updating filter: gcloud logging sinks update SINK --log-filter='false'

destructive_patterns.name: spanner-instances-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud spanner instances delete destroys a Spanner instance — all databases and data lost.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
spanner instances delete removes a Spanner instance:

- All databases inside the instance are deleted
- Data is unrecoverable unless previously exported
- Applications writing to these DBs fail immediately

Export data first: gcloud dataflow jobs run export-spanner --region=REGION  --parameters=sourceInstance=INST,destinationPath=gs://bkt/backup/

destructive_patterns.name: bigtable-instances-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud bigtable instances delete destroys a Bigtable instance — all tables and data lost.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
bigtable instances delete removes a Bigtable instance:

- All tables, clusters, and data are permanently deleted
- No backup unless one was explicitly taken
- Downstream pipelines consuming from Bigtable fail

Take a backup first: cbt -instance=INST createsnapshot CLUSTER TABLE SNAPSHOT 30

destructive_patterns.name: dataproc-clusters-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud dataproc clusters delete destroys a Dataproc (Hadoop/Spark) cluster.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
dataproc clusters delete removes a Dataproc cluster:

- Running jobs are killed
- Any data stored on local HDFS or cluster-local disks is lost
- Data in GCS (external) is preserved
- Cluster name is reserved for ~5 min; re-creation may fail until it clears

destructive_patterns.name: bq-rm-recursive
destructive_patterns.description: bq rm -r/-f removes BigQuery datasets, tables, or models — data lost.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
bq rm recursively deletes BigQuery resources:

- `bq rm -r DATASET`: removes dataset + ALL tables/views/models inside
- `bq rm -f TABLE`: removes a table without confirmation
- Data is not recoverable (unless a prior `EXPORT` or snapshot exists)
- No trash/recycle bin

Export first: bq extract --destination_format=NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON  DATASET.TABLE gs://bkt/backup/*.json
